decisions.quote: We replicate this work and then add to the exercise by examining the role that group size plays in generating social-pressure bias – an extension we motivate with a structural model. Having replicated to the extent possible the List et al.’s consequential private and public treatments, we find that when group size is large (N = 60), social isolation reduces affirmative votes by roughly 30%, a result that does not carry over to the small-group (N = 30) session.
decisions.reason: The authors confirm List et al.'s (2004) 30% reduction in affirmative voting under social isolation in the large-group replication treatment and explicitly frame the group-size variation (including the null small-group session) as an added extension motivated by a structural model rather than a failed retest of an original claim.
